questions.stem:
A car of mass 1000 kg is towing a caravan of mass 750 kg along a straight horizontal road. The caravan is connected to the car by a tow-bar which is parallel to the direction of motion of the car and the caravan. The tow-bar is modelled as a light rod. The engine of the car provides a constant driving force of 3200 N. The resistances to the motion of the car and the caravan are modelled as constant forces of magnitude 800 newtons and $R$ newtons respectively.
Given that the acceleration of the car and the caravan is $0.88\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$,

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) show that $R=860$,
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
For the whole system
$R(\rightarrow)$: $3200-800-R=1750\times 0.88$ M1 A1
Leading to $R=860$ * A1
(3)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) find the tension in the tow-bar.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
For the caravan
$R(\rightarrow)$: $T-860=750\times 0.88$ M1 A1
Leading to $T=1520$ (N) A1
(3)
Alternative for (b)
For the car
$R(\rightarrow)$: $3200-800-T=1000\times 0.88$ M1 A1
Leading to $T=1520$ (N) A1
(3)

questions.stem:
Three forces $\mathbf{F}_1$, $\mathbf{F}_2$ and $\mathbf{F}_3$ acting on a particle $P$ are given by
$\mathbf{F}_1 = (7\mathbf{i} - 9\mathbf{j})$ N
$\mathbf{F}_2 = (5\mathbf{i} + 6\mathbf{j})$ N
$\mathbf{F}_3 = (p\mathbf{i} + q\mathbf{j})$ N
where $p$ and $q$ are constants.
Given that $P$ is in equilibrium,

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) find the value of $p$ and the value of $q$.
(3)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The force $\mathbf{F}_3$ is now removed. The resultant of $\mathbf{F}_1$ and $\mathbf{F}_2$ is $\mathbf{R}$.
Find
(b) the magnitude of $\mathbf{R}$,
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\mathbf{R}=12\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j}$
$|\mathbf{R}|=\sqrt{12^2+(-3)^2}=\sqrt{153}$ or $3\sqrt{17}$ or $12.4$ or better (N) M1 A1
(2)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) the angle, to the nearest degree, that the direction of $\mathbf{R}$ makes with $\mathbf{j}$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\tan\theta=\frac{3}{12}$ M1
$\theta=14.03^\circ...$ A1
Angle with $\mathbf{j}$ is $104^\circ$, to the nearest degree cao A1
(3)

questions.stem: A non-uniform rod $AB$, of mass $m$ and length $5d$, rests horizontally in equilibrium on two supports at $C$ and $D$, where $AC = DB = d$, as shown in Figure 1. The centre of mass of the rod is at the point $G$. A particle of mass $\frac{5}{2}m$ is placed on the rod at $B$ and the rod is on the point of tipping about $D$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that $GD = \frac{5}{2}d$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M($D$): $mg\times GD=\frac{5}{2}mg\times d$ M1 A1
Leading to $GD=\frac{5}{2}d$ * DM1 A1
(4)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The particle is moved from $B$ to the mid-point of the rod and the rod remains in equilibrium.
(b) Find the magnitude of the normal reaction between the support at $D$ and the rod.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M($C$): $mg\times\frac{d}{2}+\frac{5}{2}mg\times\frac{3}{2}d=Y\times 3d$ M1 A2(1,0)
Leading to $Y=\frac{17}{12}mg$ DM1 A1
(5)

questions.stem:
A stone is projected vertically upwards from a point $A$ with speed $u\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. After projection the stone moves freely under gravity until it returns to $A$. The time between the instant that the stone is projected and the instant that it returns to $A$ is $3\frac{4}{7}$ seconds.
Modelling the stone as a particle,

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) show that $u=17\frac{1}{2}$,
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
$v=u+at(\uparrow) \Rightarrow 0=u-g\left(\frac{25}{14}\right)$ M1 M(A)1
$u=17\frac{1}{2}$ * A1
(3)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) find the greatest height above $A$ reached by the stone,
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
$v^2=u^2+2as(\uparrow) \Rightarrow 0^2=17.5^2-2gs$ M1
$s=15.6$ (m) or $16$ (m) A1
(2)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) find the length of time for which the stone is at least $6\frac{3}{5}$ m above $A$.
(6)

questions.stem:
A car moves along a straight horizontal road from a point $A$ to a point $B$, where $AB=885$ m.
The car accelerates from rest at $A$ to a speed of $15\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at a constant rate $a\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.
The time for which the car accelerates is $\frac{1}{3}T$ seconds. The car maintains the speed of $15\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ for $T$ seconds. The car then decelerates at a constant rate of $2.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ stopping at $B$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the time for which the car decelerates.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
$v=u+at \Rightarrow 0=15-2.5t$ M1
$t=6$ (s) A1
(2)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Sketch a speed-time graph for the motion of the car.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
Shape B1
$15, T$ B1
(2)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the value of $T$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\frac{1}{2}\times 15\left(\frac{4}{3}T+6+T\right)=885$ ft their 6 M1 A1ft
$\frac{7}{3}T=118-6$ M1
$T=112\times\frac{3}{7}=48$ A1
(4)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Find the value of $a$.
(2)

parts.label: e

(e) Sketch an acceleration-time graph for the motion of the car.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:

Correctly placed; no cts vert line B1
$-2.5$, ft their $\frac{15}{16}$ B1
(3)

questions.stem:
[In this question, the unit vectors $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are due east and due north respectively. Position vectors are relative to a fixed origin $O$.]
A boat $P$ is moving with constant velocity $(-4\mathbf{i}+8\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Calculate the speed of $P$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\sqrt{(-4)^2+8^2}=\sqrt{80}$ (km h$^{-1}$) accept exact equivalents or $8.9$ or better M1 A1
(2)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
When $t=0$, the boat $P$ has position vector $(2\mathbf{i}-8\mathbf{j})$ km. At time $t$ hours, the position vector of $P$ is $\mathbf{p}$ km.
(b) Write down $\mathbf{p}$ in terms of $t$.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\mathbf{p}=(2\mathbf{i}-8\mathbf{j})+t(-4\mathbf{i}+8\mathbf{j})$ B1
(1)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
A second boat $Q$ is also moving with constant velocity. At time $t$ hours, the position vector of $Q$ is $\mathbf{q}$ km, where
$\mathbf{q}=18\mathbf{i}+12\mathbf{j}-t(6\mathbf{i}+8\mathbf{j})$
Find
(c) the value of $t$ when $P$ is due west of $Q$,
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
Equating $\mathbf{j}$ components
$-8+8t=12-8t$ M1 A1
$t=\frac{5}{4}$ oe A1
(3)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) the distance between $P$ and $Q$ when $P$ is due west of $Q$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
Using their $t$ from (c) to find the i-cpts of $\mathbf{p}$ and $\mathbf{q}$ and subtract them M1
$10\frac{1}{2}-(-3)=13\frac{1}{2}$ (km) A1 ft A1
(3)

questions.stem: A particle $P$ of mass 4 kg is moving up a fixed rough plane at a constant speed of $16\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ under the action of a force of magnitude 36 N. The plane is inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The force acts in the vertical plane containing the line of greatest slope of the plane through $P$, and acts at $30^\circ$ to the inclined plane, as shown in Figure 2. The coefficient of friction between $P$ and the plane is $\mu$. Find

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the magnitude of the normal reaction between $P$ and the plane,
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
$R+36\sin 30^\circ=4g\cos 30^\circ$ M1 A1
$R\approx 15.9, 16$ M1 A1
(4)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) the value of $\mu$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
Use of $F_r=\mu R$ B1
$36\cos 30^\circ=F+4g\sin 30^\circ$ M1 A1
$\mu=\frac{36\cos 30^\circ-4g\sin 30^\circ}{R}\approx 0.726$ M1 A1
$0.73$
(5)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The force of magnitude 36 N is removed.
(c) Find the distance that $P$ travels between the instant when the force is removed and the instant when it comes to rest.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
After force is removed
$R=4g\cos 30^\circ$ B1
$-\mu 4g\cos 30^\circ-4g\sin 30^\circ=4a$
$a=(-)11.06...$ M1 A1
$v^2=u^2+2as \Rightarrow 0^2=16^2-2\times 11.06...\times s$ M1
$s=\frac{16^2}{2\times 11.06...}\approx 11.6$ (m) A1
(5)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $12$
